Author: G.Radha Rani
Bench: G.Radha Rani
 The Honourable Dr.Justice G.Radha Rani
 M.A.C.M.A.No.1888 of 2017
Judgment:

This appeal is filed by the Insurance Company aggrieved by the award and decree dated 08.11.2016 in O.P.No.107 of 2016 (Old O.P.No.144 of 2015 on the file of the Principal District Judge, Adilabad)
passed by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (for short "Tribunal")-cum-III Additional District Judge, Asifabad.
2. The parties are hereinafter referred as arrayed before the Tribunal.

3. The challenge in this O.P. was with regard to the Tribunal imposing liability on the Insurance Company without considering the fact that the charge- sheet was filed against the driver of the crime vehicle under Section 181 of the Motor Vehicles Act for not having driving license and for not apportioning the negligence in between the vehicles involved in the accident by following the principle of composite negligence.

4. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant - Insurance Company and the learned counsel for the respondent - claimant.
5.

As per the claim petition filed by the claimant, he was working as a General Mazdoor in Goleti 1A incline in Bellampally area of Dr.GRR, J macma_1888_2017 Singareni Colleries Company Limited and while he was proceeding on a motorcycle bearing No.AP1E8147 as a pillion rider from Kariguda to Bellampally and when reached near Kannala gate fly over, Bellampalli at 05:30 PM, a TATA ACE vehicle bearing No.AP01TV4319 came in an opposite direction driven by its driver with high-speed and in a rash and negligent manner, hit the motorcycle, due to which, both the rider and pillion rider fell down and sustained injuries.

The claimant claimed compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- from the respondents 1,2 and 3, the driver, owner and insurer of the TATA ACE vehicle.
6.
The respondents 1 and 2, the driver and owner of the TATA ACE vehicle remained ex-parte.
7. The respondent No.3 (appellant) contested the matter.
The respondent No.3 contended that the respondent No.1 was not having valid driving license and violated the terms and conditions of the policy and as such denied its liability.

sentences.text: The Tribunal framed two (02) specific issues on the contentions raised by the insurance company.

One, with regard to whether there was any contributory negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle or whether there was any negligence on the part of the claimant and the other, whether there was any breach of the policy conditions.
Dr.GRR, J macma_1888_2017 9.

With regard to the issue on contributory negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle, the Tribunal observed that the evidence of PW.1 and the documents marked under Ex.A1 and Ex.B1 would prove that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of TATA ACE by respondent No.1 and there was no contributory negligence on the part of the claimant.
10. With regard to the issue on breach of policy conditions, the Tribunal observed that no evidence was led by the insurance company to prove that there was any breach of any conditions of policy.

The Tribunal also answered the contention of the counsel for the insurance company with regard to the charge- sheet filed against the driver of the TATA ACE under Section 181 of the Motor Vehicles Act and observed that though Section 181 of the Motor Vehicles Act was quoted in the charge-sheet,
it was only an allegation in the charge-sheet which had to be proved by adducing evidence, but no evidence was adduced by respondent No.3 to prove the said allegation.

As such, basing on the mere allegation in the charge-sheet, observed that it could not be held that respondent No.1 had no valid driving license and that respondent No.2 had knowledge about the said fact and handed over the TATA ACE to respondent No.1 with the said knowledge.

The Tribunal further observed that as such respondent No.3 could not escape its liability and held the respondents 1 to 3 jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation of Rs.2,84,000/- awarded to the Dr.GRR, J macma_1888_2017 claimant with interest @ 9 % per annum for the injuries sustained by him in the road accident.
11. Aggrieved by the said award and decree, the insurance company preferred this appeal.
12. As observed by the Tribunal, the respondent No.3 - Insurance Company had not adduced any oral evidence to prove its contentions.
Ex. B1, the attested copy of the charge-sheet was marked by consent.
The charge-sheet was filed against the driver of the TATA ACE vehicle bearing No.AP01TV4319 under Section 338 of IPC read with Section 181 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
It was mentioned in the charge-sheet that the driver of the TATA ACE vehicle without holding valid driving license was driving the vehicle and caused the accident.
13. A charge-sheet is not a substantive piece of evidence.
The Sub-Inspector of Police, who filed the charge-sheet, would need to be examined to prove its contents.

Without adducing any oral evidence,
the insurance company could not ask the Tribunal to base its observations on the contents of the charge-sheet.

14. Even with regard to the aspect of deciding the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the TATA ACE vehicle or there was any contributory negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle, the contents of the charge-sheet are taken as a corroborative piece of evidence to the oral Dr.GRR, J macma_1888_2017 evidence adduced before the Tribunal by the claimant, who was United India Insurance Company Limited vs Poludasari Kumuraiah And 2 Others on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116807350/

15. The contents of the charge-sheet alone cannot be relied upon to accept it as a substantive piece of evidence.

The insurance company ought to have examined the respondents 1 and 2, the driver and owner of the TATA ACE vehicle or ought to have examined the investigating officer, who filed the charge-sheet to prove that the respondent No.1 was not holding a valid driving license at the time of the accident.

16. Likewise, this Court also finds no merit in the contention of the learned counsel for the insurance company with regard to the negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle, as no evidence was adduced by the insurance company in this regard.
The police records like FIR and charge-sheet corroborated the evidence of PW.1 on the aspect of the negligence on the part of the driver of the TATA ACE vehicle.

17. As such, this Court does not find any merit in the contention of the learned counsel for the appellant - Insurance Company to order for "pay and recovery" for violation of conditions of the policy or to exonerate the insurance company from discharging its liability.
18. In the result, the appeal filed by the Insurance Company is dismissed.
No order as to costs.
Dr.GRR, J macma_1888_2017
As a sequel, miscellaneous applications pending in this appeal, if any, shall stand closed.
Dr. G. RADHA RANI, J Date: 19th July, 2023 Nsk.
